clues: This city sits on the banks of a river in flat plains, a long way north east of Warsaw.
Summers here are warm. But winters are long and full of frost, a sharp change in the year.
The first folk came in the 1300s. The town did not get its charter till 1692, quite late in its tale.
Its east side meets Belarus. That line is the east edge of the European Union and the Schengen lands.
Woods fill close to one fifth of this city. It ranks fifth for woods among all big towns in Poland.
